map.夜间血压下降率评估：输入昼/夜收缩压均值，判断杓型（下降 10%–20%）、非杓: Nighttime blood pressure drop rate assessment: enter the daytime and nighttime systolic means and classify the dipper pattern (10%–20% drop), non-dipper (<10%) or extreme dipper (>20%), which helps identify autonomic and blood pressure rhythm abnormalities.
map.晨峰血压计算：取起床后 2 小时平均收缩压与夜间最低收缩压（或睡眠谷值）之差，差: Morning surge blood pressure calculation: take the difference between the mean systolic pressure 2 hours after rising and the lowest nighttime systolic pressure (or the sleep trough); a difference ≥35 mmHg indicates an excessive morning surge, which is associated with morning cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events.
map.晨峰血压高有什么意义？: What Does a High Morning Surge Blood Pressure Mean?
map.晨起交感神经激活使血压快速上升，晨峰过大（一般取起床后 2h 均值减夜间最低值: Sympathetic activation on waking makes blood pressure rise quickly, and an excessive morning surge (generally the 2h post-waking mean minus the nighttime minimum ≥35 mmHg) is associated with the risk of morning myocardial infarction and stroke. Controlling the morning surge requires regular medication and attention to dosing times, with the specifics decided individually by a physician.

map.白大衣与隐匿性高血压鉴别：对比诊室血压与 24h 动态均值，诊室高而动态正常为白: Differentiating white-coat from masked hypertension: compare the office blood pressure with the 24h ambulatory mean; high in the office but normal on ambulatory monitoring is white-coat hypertension, while normal in the office but elevated on monitoring is masked hypertension, which guides whether to start medication.
map.监测日保持日常活动，避免剧烈运动与长时间卧床；袖带绑在非优势臂上臂，充气时手臂放: On the monitoring day keep normal activities and avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged bed rest; wrap the cuff on the upper arm of the non-dominant arm and let the arm hang relaxed during inflation; record sleep and wake times so the daytime and night-time periods can be distinguished. The measurements are for trend reference only.
map.通常定义下降 10%–20% 为杓型（正常节律）；<10% 为非杓型，>20%: A drop of 10%–20% is usually defined as a dipper (normal rhythm); <10% is a non-dipper and >20% an extreme dipper or reverse dipper, the latter being more common in diabetes, sleep apnoea and some older populations and being associated with higher cardiovascular risk.
